headline: Executive order directing federal agencies to limit criminal penalties for breaking federal regulations.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order deals with federal rules that can carry criminal penalties, such as fines or jail time, when broken. It aims to reduce what it calls overcriminalization by changing how agencies write and enforce these rules. No summary was provided, so the specific steps it requires are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that write and enforce regulations
who_it_affects.how: They would likely have to change how they create rules that carry criminal penalties and how they enforce them.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses and individuals who must follow federal regulations
who_it_affects.how: They could face a lower risk of criminal charges for breaking regulatory rules, depending on how agencies carried out the order.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed January 18, 2021; no separate effective date was provided.
